one_line_contribution: On ALFWorld with a fixed six-procedure trajectory bank, the claim is that whole-bank-in-context reading is indifferent to prompt length and redundancy but degrades with the number of cross-type near-miss (same object+receptacle, different procedure) trajectories, while top-k retrieval's twin exposure is capped by k and therefore flat in bank count at fixed near-miss share, yielding a route x composition interaction at matched length that grows for a weaker reader.
closest_prior_work: Two verified threats. (1) arXiv:2605.10828, 'The First Drop of Ink: Nonlinear Impact of Misleading Information in Long-Context Reasoning' (2026-05-11, verified via s2cli paper) already does the proposal's core separation in the home literature: it varies hard-distractor PROPORTION inside FIXED-LENGTH contexts and finds a sharp nonlinear drop concentrated in the first small fraction, then near-saturation. That is 'confusable, not long' already measured, and it is worse than a novelty threat: because the N ladder pins near-miss share at 0.5 at every size (12/24/48/80), the whole ladder sits past that paper's knee, so the leading published mechanism predicts WB is FLAT in count on the N ladder, i.e. P2's monotonic decline and P4's interaction fail while WB(N-80)-WB(R-80) may still be negative. The proposal never cites or searched for this paper. (2) arXiv:2405.00200 (verified, NAACL 2025, 157 citations) already establishes that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the nearest demonstrations rather than cumulative encoding, which independently predicts P1 (flat under redundant/filler growth) and the direction of P2; the proposal concedes this and can only claim the transfer to trajectories and task success. arXiv:2608.22695 (Enrich-Retrieve-Rank, verified) is correctly identified as the nearest agentic analogue and is genuinely different (distinct options, Match@1, one router), so it is not the binding threat. What survives as new is narrow: the count-vs-share dissociation of the two routes on agent task success.
strongest_objection: The headline count law is not identified, and the headline contrast is underpowered at the stated threshold. (a) Count and coverage are entangled by construction: N-12 has ~6 twin pairs and N-80 has ~40, so the fraction of the 274 test goals whose combo has a twin in the bank rises with size. Any WB decline across the N ladder is then plausibly 'more episodes have a confusable twin present at all', not 'more confusable items hurt a fixed episode' - and the same growth breaks P3b's fixed-share premise for retrieval, since per-episode twin exposure in the top-3 is coverage-bound, not share-bound. The proposal admits this in Risk Factors and offers only a descriptive covered/uncovered split, i.e. it declines to manipulate the variable its title is about. (b) P4 and P5 are double and triple differences judged at the same 9-net threshold calibrated for single paired contrasts at 274x2 (the brief's own floor is +/-8 net for a single contrast); a difference of differences carries roughly 1.4-2x that SE, so a true -9 interaction cannot be separated from 0 at a 90% bootstrap CI. The confirmatory arm of the headline is therefore powered only for effects near -15 or larger, while the falsifier region is wide - a design that can much more easily report 'no interaction' than establish one. (c) N and R banks differ in item identity as well as twin share; RET-T bounds this for the retrieval route only, and the proposal states there is no whole-bank analogue, so the WB half of P2/P4 - the half that carries the claim - has no identity control. (d) P6 compares WB(U-80) against RET k=3 over the full 1,465-item pool, a different bank, so any breach confounds route with bank size.
what_would_fix_it: Rebuild the N ladder so coverage is constant: construct every N size so that each of the 274 test goals' combos has exactly one twin pair present (coverage = 1.0 at N-12 through N-80) and grow the count only with twin pairs for combos that do not occur in the test set. Then count varies at fixed share AND fixed per-episode exposure, and P2/P3b/P4 test the count law rather than a coverage law; report the ladder in exposure terms (twins per episode) as well as bank size. Second, add a share axis at fixed count (e.g. 80 items at near-miss share 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) so the design can distinguish the proportional/saturating law of 2605.10828 from the count law the title asserts - as written, the two are only compared at share 0 vs 0.5. Third, compute and pre-register the MDE for the P4 double difference and the P5 triple difference separately (they are not 9 net) and add seeds, or restate P4 as a comparison of two separately-powered simple contrasts. Fourth, add a WB identity control: relabel the twins' task types in the WB prefix (same items, twin-ness removed) so the WB route gets the analogue of RET-T. Fifth, state the truncation rule when an 80-item prefix (~11k tokens) plus a long ALFWorld rollout history exceeds 16k mid-episode; the brief demands this and the proposal does not give it. Finally, cite and position against 2605.10828 - a proposal titled 'Confusable, Not Long' that has not found the paper that measured confusable-vs-long has not established novelty.
missing_baseline: RET k=3 over U-80 itself. P6 pits a whole-bank arm on an 80-item random subset against retrieval over the 1,465-item pool, so route and bank size move together and the prediction cannot come out cleanly; retrieval over exactly the same 80 items is the arm a reviewer will demand and it costs one 548-episode cell. Secondary: a WB arm on N-80 with twin items' type labels made explicit (or twins' procedure headers annotated), which separates 'the reader cannot tell twins apart' from 'the reader is distracted by extra items' and is the WB counterpart of RET-T that the proposal says does not exist.
preprint_collision: No verified collision on the full claim, but the proposal's check is materially incomplete on the mechanism half. Queries I ran, all through the s2cli literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both channels ok; WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch never used): (1) 'confusable near-duplicate demonstrations in context distractor examples degrade long context agent' -> arXiv:2605.10828, 2510.07414 (HaystackCraft, agentic distractor robustness), 2405.00200, 2501.12766, 2503.23306. (2) 'whole bank in context versus top-k retrieval agent trajectory memory crossover bank size task success' --recent -> arXiv:2608.22695, 2607.26637, 2607.13591, 2607.10608, 2605.18421 (EvoMemBench: long-context baselines still outperform specialized memory methods), 2603.02473, 2605.12493. (3) 'Enrich-Retrieve-Rank in-context routing registry scaling collapse retrieve-then-rank capability discovery' -> arXiv:2608.22695 plus unrelated router/MoE work (2606.07587, 2605.08292, 2506.22262), confirming the proposal's read of its closest named method. (4) 'similar but wrong exemplars misleading demonstrations agent copies wrong procedure ALFWorld experience reuse' --recent -> 2609.02217, 2606.26669, 2605.29463, 2607.20891; nothing that grows confusable trajectories in a bank. (5) 'number of distractors versus context length controlled separation retrieval versus long context degradation' --recent -> arXiv:2605.10828 again, 2506.08184 (proactive interference beyond context length), 2505.06914, 2502.05167. (6) 'retrieval more robust than in-context reading to distractors interaction between retrieval and context composition' -> 2605.10828, 2505.15561, 2607.00725; no paper runs the route x composition interaction. Verified by id with s2cli paper: 2608.22695, 2405.00200, 2411.07130, 2510.16809, 2607.26497, 2603.04814, 2605.24117, 2412.16926, 2411.05000, 2607.10608, 2605.10828, 2605.18421 - all resolve and match the proposal's descriptions where cited. I did not verify 2607.02255, 2606.22844, 2605.05191, 2603.04257, 2602.01566, 2404.11018, 2408.13987, 2506.04579, 2605.03644, 2502.09933 (not load-bearing for novelty). Judgment on the proposal's check: it is unusually well documented for its structure - four classed queries, channels named, the closest method identified and characterized correctly - but it is thin on outcome, because the single most pre-emptive recent preprint on 'confusable, not long' (2605.10828, 2026-05, cited) was missed by every one of its queries, which used agent/memory/bank vocabulary or many-shot ICL vocabulary but never 'distractor proportion at fixed length'. Two further recent items its recency query should have surfaced and engaged, 2605.18421 (long-context baselines beating memory systems) and 2506.08184 (proactive interference as a length-independent limit), also bear directly on the hypothesis. The check therefore establishes that the exact agentic experiment is unrun, not that the mechanism claim is new.
